Contact center · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Risk-based QA sampling

Leticia · Contact Center QA Specialist

In an operation with 280 service seats, four QA monitors evaluate 6 calls per agent per month, which covers 0.4% of volume and is drawn at random with no criteria.

When it runs
Monthly, at the turn of the quality cycle, to draw the month's sample, and every two weeks for the calibration session among monitors on a common set of calls
What it delivers in production
Every month, the risk-stratified sample with a guaranteed quota per agent and a pre-read of each call, and every two weeks the divergence report among monitors per scorecard item, with the criteria to rewrite.
Who decides
Samples and pre-reads; the monitor evaluates
Effort
Calibrate on 30 complaint calls; two monthly cycles
Set up5 steps · 6 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

# QA scorecard and risk matrix (excerpt)

## QA scorecard (scores from 0 to 100 per item)
| Item | Criterion | Weight | Compliance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Greeting and agent identification | 5 | no |
| 3 | Listening and probing the need | 15 | no |
| 7 | Full reading of the total effective cost (CET) before acceptance | 25 | yes, zeroes the score |
| 12 | Identity check with full CPF (individual tax ID) and date of birth | 25 | yes, zeroes the score |
| 15 | Courtesy and closing | 10 | no |

Spread limit: an item with a spread above 15 points gets a recommendation to rewrite the criterion.

## Risk matrix (signals)
| Signal | Rule |
|---|---|
| S1 | signup call with max_silence_s above 90 |
| S2 | repeat_7d = yes |
| S3 | ticket with a complaint in complaints.csv |
| S4 | cancellation with 2 or more transfers |

## Minimum quota
2 calls per active agent in the cycle.

## Rules with no leeway
- The agent's quota takes the 2 calls with no signal and the lowest ticket numbers. E.g. OP-11 gets C-5002 and C-5005, not C-5018. OP-14 has only C-5014: it enters and coverage is incomplete (1 of 2).
- The limit is strict: 90 seconds of silence is not S1 and 1 transfer is not S4. E.g. C-5009 and C-5010 have no signal. The complaint for C-9999, which is not in calls.csv, is ignored.
- Spread only compares monitors on the same calibration call. E.g. C-4700 has a single monitor and stays out; the empty score in C-4803 stays out and is recorded; item 12 = 100 - 70 = 30 in C-4801.
- An agent with 3 or more calls with a signal goes to the supervisor, whichever quota the call is in. E.g. OP-11 with C-5001, C-5003, C-5004 and C-5015 = 4.
- The customer's CPF, name and phone number appear nowhere in the output, not even in the pre-read excerpt. E.g. the CPF the customer says in C-5001 stays out; quote another excerpt.

## Excluded content
Whatever a rule says to exclude or hide appears nowhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If it must be recorded, write only "content excluded by rule", without repeating it.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI does not assign scores or replace the monitor: the pre-read points to excerpts and items, and the person evaluates, because the score feeds variable pay and disciplinary processes. Using the pre-read as an evaluation when the monitor has not listened to the call is forbidden, and so is building the risk quota in a way that leaves any agent without an evaluated call in the month. Transcripts and recordings are restricted to quality, in line with the LGPD (Brazil's data protection law). A compliance item that zeros the score is never decided by the automatic transcript alone.

Common mistakes

  • Drawing the sample uniformly over the operation's volume; QA ends up concentrated on short, simple, lower-risk calls.
  • Discussing the agent's score in the calibration session among monitors, which exists to measure disagreement between them.
  • Treating high divergence as the monitor's failure rather than the criterion's; the criterion is almost always written ambiguously.
  • Evaluating a compliance item only from the automatic transcript; line noise degrades recognition precisely in the mandatory reading passages.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
QA coverage of volumefrom 0.4% to the 0.8% to 1.2% range without hiring monitors, by cutting selection timeestimate based on the described routine
Score spread between monitors on the same callfrom 18 points to below 8 points after four calibration sessionsestimate based on the described routine
Calls that generated complaints captured by the risk quota60% or more of the 30 calls in the historical testcalibration threshold agreed with the area, estimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Quality cycle 09/2026. Month's volume: 214,000 calls. Sample: 1,680 calls (0.8%).
SAMPLE COMPOSITION
  quota per agent: 4 calls per active agent (1,120 calls)
  high-risk quota: 560 calls by signal | product sign-up with silence above 90 seconds: 148 | calls with a 7-day repeat call: 201 | tickets with a complaint recorded in any channel: 96 | cancellation with a double transfer: 115
PRE-READ (example) | ticket 88-441902 | sign-up queue | duration 11m32s | attention on items 7 (reading of the total effective cost) and 12 (identity confirmation). Excerpt at 04m11s: the customer interrupts the reading and the agent moves on to the confirmation.
CALIBRATION FOR THE FORTNIGHT (5 calls, 4 monitors)
  item 12, identity confirmation: a 25-point spread between monitors. Ambiguous criterion on partial confirmation.
  item 7, mandatory reading: an 8-point spread (+1 identical: posture and courtesy items, a 3-point spread)
  RECOMMENDATION: rewrite the criterion for item 12 before the next cycle.
